page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core running at 2.8 GHz, with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.0 GB per core memory allocation. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers of overall compute capacity. The stress-ng single-core benchmark scores 1399.29, while the multi-core test yields 1841.88, reflecting its limited physical core count. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block transfers reaching 13.72 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 11.78 GB/sec. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1111.0 and a multi-core score of 1311.0, indicating weak to poor performance relative to larger hardware profiles.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources but have minimal memory requirements. The 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it highly resource-dense for CPU-bound tasks that do not demand large memory footprints, though users must accept the trade-off of lower absolute performance.

This instance is best suited for lightweight, CPU-focused workloads such as basic static web serving, simple text processing, and small-scale background tasks. It can also handle minor database operations and low-demand utility scripting where memory overhead is strictly controlled.
